audit: 2026-11-19 calls, lifecycle and the night's work (0.5.0 -> 0.6 work)
baseline: 0.5.0 (96837b7) plus the classic-call work of the night (a93f0b3..1156f09)
method: Six read-only agents (Rust core, C++ bridge, QML and UX, security and privacy, tests/docs/build, the abort on quit with gdb on the Jolla Phone 2026), triage with an advisor, fixes in batches built and installed on the Jolla Phone 2026 and the Pro1-X. See 2026-11-19-calls-and-lifecycle.md.

findings.summary: Every quit since 0.4.7 aborted (exit 134): Core::shutdown made its tokio timeout on Qt's main thread, outside the runtime; the panic could not leave the extern "C" rustrx_shutdown. Session save, store pause, ordered bus-name release and the stand-in start after closing never ran; lipstick crashed in the same second several times.
findings.test: core test shutdown_outside_the_runtime_finishes (fails on the old line: 'there is no reactor running'); jp26: dev quit -> exit(0), no lipstick crash

findings.summary: The call's Connections block was inserted inside the one for rustrx: push notifications, knocks, closing a ringing call's notification and the quit request did nothing in test builds 0.5.0-2 to -13 (no release had it).
VoipPage used Tunables without importing the Rustrx module: a ReferenceError at the call's end on the phone (found by grepping the -18 log; qmllint does not see it).
findings.test: static test_qml_that_uses_tunables_imports_them; -19 on both phones: no QML errors since start

findings.summary: Any member of any room could ring every member's phone; the sender's invite lifetime was uncapped (past INT_MAX the ring never stopped, real calls dropped as busy).
